P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: Compression codec performance (especially on low-power devices in mesh mode). Template lookup latency (should be negligible with static registry). Delta encoding complexity for highly variable custom messages. Decompression on large message batches (offline sync).
P.P2_defensibility: Templates pre-compose common emergency messages (safe, privacy-friendly). Compression reduces mesh bandwidth by 80%+ (critical for intermittent connectivity). 2-byte codes for template messages are extremely efficient. Fallback to plaintext for custom messages (no loss of functionality).
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence in template system (lookup is trivial). High confidence in 2-byte template codes (proven technique). Medium confidence in delta encoding compression (tuning needed for custom messages).
P4_failure_modes: Template key not found → fallback to plaintext (safe, but defeats optimization)
Compression fails on malformed input → message not sent (mitigate: try uncompressed fallback)
Decompression failure on receive → message unreadable (mitigate: flag corrupted message, ask user to resend)
Context variables not substituted → template shows '{location}' instead of actual location (mitigate: sanitize templates, test before deploy)
P.P5_backup_plan: If compression unavailable: send uncompressed (higher mesh bandwidth). If decompression fails: show raw message and ask resend. If template not found: use template_key as fallback display (user sees technical code).
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate compression failure (mock codec error). Test decompression failure (corrupt payload). Test template not found (reference invalid key). Test context variable failure (missing location, null status).
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for template lookup. Unit tests for compression/decompression (test vectors). Integration tests for compression in mesh mode. Load tests for compression on 1000 messages. End-to-end tests for template message flow. Stress test: custom messages with 10k characters (extreme delta encoding).
P.P8_benchmarks: Template lookup: <50ms. Compression (template): 1 message → 2 bytes. Compression (custom): 80%+ ratio vs plaintext. Decompression: <50ms per message. Compression CPU: <5% on device. Mesh bandwidth: 80%+ reduction vs uncompressed.

L.L1_legal_considerations: Templates are system-provided. No legal risk from templates themselves. Custom messages inherit same encryption and legal protections as regular messages.
L.L3_consent_requirements: Users implicitly consent to template use by selecting them. No separate consent.
L.L4_liability_notes: None significant. Templates are optional (user can type custom message). Template wording must be neutral and non-discriminatory.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Template registry: ~10KB static data. Compression CPU: negligible (client-side, algorithm-limited). No API or storage costs.
F.F2_accounting_considerations: Operational cost (client runtime), no special accounting.
F.F3_revenue_impact: Compression enables mesh networking (key differentiator). Improves offline experience and user satisfaction.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Template codes are predictable (feature, not vulnerability). Compression happens before encryption (compression is metadata operation). No security added by encryption after compression (payload already entropy-reduced).
S.S2_data_privacy: Templates may reveal message intent (template code in plaintext before encryption). Acceptable risk (adversary can infer intent anyway). Custom messages encrypted same as all messages.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Templates encrypted same as messages: Signal Protocol or AES-256-GCM
S.S4_access_control: Templates public (everyone uses same templates). Custom message compression per-user (each message has own encoded state).
S.S5_audit_requirements: Log when templates are used (for analytics, not security).

X.X1_notes: Templates are key to mesh efficiency. Emergency messages (safe, need help, evacuating) are critical use cases. 2-byte codes reduce bandwidth from ~1KB to 2 bytes (500x improvement). Pre-composed messages reduce user cognitive load during crisis. Context substitution (location, status) keeps messages personalized.
X2_open_questions: Template taxonomy? (status, help request, evacuation, all-clear, etc.)
Which context variables to support? (location, timestamp, group name, status?)
Custom message compression or only templates? (custom adds complexity, but helps offline)
X.X3_related_research: Huffman coding. Varint encoding (protobuf). LZ4 compression. Delta encoding. Mesh protocol literature. Emergency communication studies.
